summary: Adds a cloud-neutral, tenant-bound secret broker contract and write-only secret administration for segregated tenant SSO providers.
userImpact: Tenant administrators can rotate their own OIDC, SAML, and LDAP secret material without receiving secret values back from the API.
Existing encrypted, environment, file, and Docker secret references remain supported without configuration changes.

instructions: Existing deployments require no action and continue to use their configured local secret provider.
Cloud pooled deployments configure the private tenant secret broker endpoint and its workload authentication reference before accepting broker-backed tenant SSO secrets.

configuration: Adds private tenant secret broker endpoint, workload authentication reference, request timeout, bounded cache lifetime, and cloud-required availability settings.
Broker authentication material is resolved only through the existing environment, file, or Docker providers to prevent recursive secret resolution.

changes: Adds tenant-scoped write-only SSO secret put, rotate, availability, and retire operations.
Adds the tenant-secret reference contract, which binds every reference to a tenant and an allowed SSO purpose.

notes: No schema change is required because identity-provider configuration continues to persist only opaque references.

security: Every broker operation is bound to the authenticated tenant, an allowlisted purpose, an opaque reference, and a correlation identifier.
Secret values are accepted only on write, excluded from responses, audit metadata, exports, and errors, and isolated by tenant during rotation and retirement.
Broker outages fail tenant authentication safely; independently configured local references remain available as an audited operational recovery path.
documentation: Documents the broker port, tenant-secret reference grammar, SSO purpose mapping, rotation lifecycle, outage behavior, compatibility, and cloud adapter boundary.
knownLimitations: OSS provides the broker contract and authenticated private HTTP adapter; cloud-vendor secret-manager implementations remain outside the OSS repository.
rollback: Stop accepting tenant-secret references and restore affected providers to their previous encrypted, environment, file, or Docker references before rolling back the application.
Keep the broker available until no persisted provider configuration references broker-managed material.
validation: Tests cover cross-tenant denial, purpose binding, write-only responses, cache invalidation, isolated rotation, retirement, safe outage behavior, and secret-free diagnostics.
Pooled end-to-end qualification continues to exercise distinct OIDC, SAML, and LDAP providers per tenant.
